Hi everyone.
Is it possible to deal with arrays or similar in RPG Maker MZ?
I am especially referring to adding a value to a text array stored as variable.
I used to store text value in a variable using the script field and putting the value under quotes; but what if i want to add a new letter to this value?
I need this because I want to implement in my project a room where there are tiles on the floor with the letters of the alphabet: player has to "write" words by passing over the correct tiles, and this would be very easy to do if every new letter could be easily added to the others. I know this could be done in other ways, too, but with a lot of work and using of variables and/or swithces, especially if I wanto to make this thing a repeatable event (with, say, a dozen different words).
Any help?

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
You can put arrays into Game Variables. The game will not crash, but you should pay some attention.
I recommend using arrays only to those with some knowledge of JavaScript, but when you have, here you go!
To initialize an array, do Variable OP, select "Script", and input
[ ]
To add an element, you should use "Script" instead of "Variable OP", and type this:
Code:
$gameVariables.value(1).push(2)
To query for some element, you can always type
Code:
$gameVariables.value(1)[2]
To get element 2 of the array of Game Variable 1

posts.author: ISC
posts.body:
You could use the concatenation operator.
Let me give you an example. Let's say I have the word "car," and the player steps on the letter "s," creating the word "cars."
To do this, I'll show you an example in JavaScript:
```
let example = "car";
example += "s";
console.log(example); // output: cars
```
How do we translate this to RPG Maker?
Let’s say your variable 1 is equal to "car."
The player steps on the letter "S."
Variable 1 + (script) "s"
Now your variable will be equal to "cars."
However, I want to warn you about something important. The Visustella multi-language plugin doesn’t work with words defined in this way. So, if you want to make a multilingual game using the Visustella plugin, you won’t be able to, as it doesn’t work with variables containing strings (or at least I haven’t been able to make it work).

Hey everyone,
now I am dealing with how to remove the last element of my array/string.
I have declared a variable as a string with var1 = [ ]
Then I am adding element with $gameVariables.value(1) + "a"
After putting some characters in it, how can I remove the last one?
I've been trying JavaScript commands like pop, lenght or slice, bot I only got some weird results. Probably I am also messing up things with JS's syntax...
Any help?
Thanks in advice!

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
At this point, it is probably the most efficient to google "javascript how to remove last element of an array/last character of a string". You will find many pages that describe all possible operations on arrays and strings.
To remove last element of an array:
Code:
$gameVariables.value(1).pop()
Replace 1 with your Variable ID
To remove last character of a string:
Code:
const string = $gameVariables.value(1)
$gameVariables.setValue(1, string.substring(0, string.length - 1))
Again, replace the two 1s that you see in the $gameVariables function,
but keep the last 1 next to string.length as it is
.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
To add - you're starting with an empty array
[]
, but that gets converted to a blank string when you try to add a string to it:
[] + "a"
->
"" + "a"
->
"a"
.
So you would use
@Aerosys
's string example, or change your approach to use an array.

Or you can forget $gameVariables and use something like $gameSystem.variables to make your own variable list.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Learning how to use Arrays has opened up a whole world of possibilities for me. I highly recommend searching for some RPG Maker tutorials that give examples of using Arrays and you can check out a free online course like W3Schools for JavaScript and you will find lots of useful information. I also just search for specific JavaScript questions and can usually find what I need.
I have some tutorials that highlight different uses of Arrays. My tutorials progressed as I learned more about how to use Arrays and some of those tutorials specifically mention Arrays in the tutorial title or description.
My current Sudoku project uses a LOT of Arrays. For instance, right now, I am using an Array of stored data that I can pull out and use in a Variable to identify other specific Arrays and I use other Variables to identify the position location of the value I want in the appropriate Array. So my script is using Variables to identify both the Array I need to pull data from and the position of that data in the Array.
And 3 years ago, I had zero experience with RPG Maker, programming, and JavaScript.
My best advise is to take a step back, watch a bunch of tutorials and recreate the Array portions yourself in a test project. Read about Arrays and how they are used in a free JavaScript resource and recreate those functions in your test project. Then use your test project to experiment with what specifically you want to do at this time.
Because learning as much as you can about Arrays now, how they work in MZ, all the things you can do with them, will probably greatly expand your options going forward.
And this forum is great for specific questions.
Good luck and embrace the power of the Array!

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Like Robro says, the core
$gameVariables.value
method returns 0 for
falsy
values, e.g. a blank string.
An empty array is still truthy, so that would be a valid workaround. If you want to display the contents of an array as a string, you can still do so using
Array#join
:
JavaScript:
$gameVariables.value(1).join("");
E.g. if variable 1 had the value
["a", "b", "c"]
, the above code would return
"abc"
.
However, I think I'd just use a branch for "is variable = 0", like you've already done.
